content: The SIVA1 apoptosis regulatory protein, known as Siva, is a protein in humans encoded by the SIVA1 gene. This gene produces a protein that plays a critical role in the apoptotic pathway, specifically in programmed cell death triggered by the CD27 antigen. CD27 is a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor (TNFR) superfamily. The cytoplasmic tail of the CD27 antigen interacts with the N-terminal region of the Siva protein. Additionally, two alternatively spliced transcript variants of the SIVA1 gene have been identified, which encode distinct protein isoforms. SIVA1 has been experimentally shown to interact directly with the CD27 antigen. The Siva protein is an intracellular ligand that contains zinc and interacts with the CD4 receptor. It facilitates apoptosis in T-lymphoid cells induced by the HIV-1 envelope. Recent studies have revealed that Siva is a direct transcriptional target of the tumor suppressor proteins p53 and E2F1.
